chapter: Oliver's circle and old New Orleans players
title: Freddie Keppard's power and Joe Oliver's mute effects
summary: Keppard blasted the big Dreamland band, while Oliver used big hands and mutes for effects like the baby cry on Eccentric.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Oh yeah, he's about the strongest of all the fellas. Joe Oliver was strong. But you see Joe Oliver, he did a whole lot of playing mutes. Joe Oliver had large hands. And at that time the mute that he was using was just about this long. You see his hand was covered in mute. And he had all kinds of different effects. He used to feature a tune called eccentric. It had a lot of breaks in it. And Bill Johnson, whenever he'd have it, quack, quack, quack, Bill Johnson would say don't cry baby, don't cry baby. And he'd play the baby when the baby was peaceful and cooing. And then he'd have another effect when the baby started to cry, wheeh, wheeh, something like that. Well it's Harmon's mute you know. The guy got the idea from that. And Bobby Miller was giving the credit for that, but Joe Oliver was the first to do it. And he played open but a lot of times just a little mute.
But did he really put any of that down on the record where it sounds like he did? I never heard him recall that.
Yeah, yeah, yeah. This eccentric and some other tunes.
And he would get the rooster crow or anything like that?

Yeah, yeah, rooster and all that stuff. Yeah. Eccentric was one of the principal tunes I'd say. And he really could get the effect. Well Freddie, he played open a lot. And it was a difference of, now there was another fellow by the name of Jimmy Strode from here too. He worked out of the stockyard, was lugging that beef, and he caught TB and he died. And then we had a fellow named, see what it was? Jimmy who?
